answers.explanation: Angiosperms and gymnosperms are both seed plants, which belong to the group Spermatophyta.
Fungi cannot make their own food, so they are non-green plants.
Stinging cells are found in coelenterates such as Hydra.
Pteridophytes such as ferns have true roots, stems and leaves, unlike algae and bryophytes.
Lenticels are the openings through which breathing roots exchange gases.
The annulus of a fern sporangium helps to spring open and disperse the spores.
Cilia enable Paramecium to move through water, which is an adaptation to its environment.
The cocoon of the earthworm is secreted by the clitellum.
The maxillipeds of the crayfish help to hold and feed food.
The land snail breathes through a lung formed from its mantle.
Gill rakers strain food particles from the water, which helps fish in feeding.
Maize roots have a wide pith surrounded by a ring of conducting tissue.
Starch is formed from the sugar produced in photosynthesis.
The liver is an accessory organ of digestion that produces bile.
Hydrogen is present in protein, carbohydrate and lipid molecules.
The crown of the mammalian tooth is covered by enamel.
With too little oxygen, glucose is broken down into lactic acid instead of carbon dioxide and water.
Reduced humidity increases the rate of transpiration by making the air less saturated.
Water moves through a semi-permeable membrane by osmosis.
Fibrinogen and prothrombin are plasma proteins that take part in the clotting of blood.
Deoxygenated blood flows to the lungs through the pulmonary artery.
Resin is an excretory product of plants.
A taxis is the movement of a whole organism in response to an external stimulus.
The epididymis stores sperm while they mature.
An aggregate fruit is a collection of small fruits, such as achenes, formed from several separate carpels of one flower.
Vegetative propagation does not involve the reproductive organs, so it is asexual.
Gibberellin stimulates stem elongation, so it can make a dwarf plant grow to normal height.
Gregor Mendel laid the foundations of genetics through his work on inheritance in peas.
Crossing over is the exchange of genetic material between homologous chromosomes.
The dominant trait appears in both the F1 and F2 generations when heterozygotes are crossed.
River blindness is caused by a worm and is not a sex-linked character.
The physical and biotic environment are the most important factors influencing an organism's way of life.
Organisms in an ecosystem are grouped by trophic level as producers and consumers.
A food web is more stable because each organism has alternative food sources.
In the dry season the trees of a deciduous forest shed their leaves, leaving the ground bare.
Teeth are not specifically an adaptation for life in trees, unlike a tail, claws and camouflage.
Tuberculosis can be prevented by immunisation with BCG vaccine.
Industrial chimneys and the burning of fossil fuels release air pollutants.
Fertilisers are lost from soil by leaching, underground seepage and run-off.
Nitrogen-fixing bacteria live symbiotically in the root nodules of leguminous plants.
